caption: We bought the inverter so the lights would stay on. Why is our electricity still our third biggest bill?

slides.title:
What keeping the
lights on costs us
on R36 400 p/m
Living in Bronkhorstspruit
slides.body:
Him 41, her 38
Married, two kids (11 and 7)
Jobs: Boilermaker & school bookkeeper
Combined net: R36 400 p/m
Home: a three bedroom with a small solar and battery setup

slides.title: Bond repayment
slides.body: We bought before rates went up. If we bought today we'd be renting.

slides.title: Solar & inverter instalment
slides.body: It was R96 000 up front. I'm paying the finance on it, and I'd do it again, mostly.

slides.title: Electricity & water
slides.includes: Prepaid top-ups, borehole pump, municipal water
slides.body: We still buy prepaid on cloudy weeks. The solar did not make this line disappear.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Family of four, school lunch boxes
slides.body: Two kids who eat like four. I've given up arguing with the receipt.

slides.title: Fuel & car instalment
slides.includes: My bakkie to the plant, her Polo to school
slides.body: I drive 38 km each way. Nobody at the dinner table is allowed to bring this up.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: school fees and uniforms, medical aid, black tax, funeral policy, stokvel, DStv and fibre, airtime
slides.body: Seven lines I don't see individually. Together they're R8 700, and the black tax is R1 500 of it.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R36 400. We had R3 000 left before the inverter. Now the buffer is gone and the lights are on.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
We uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it picked out every electricity top-up.

We thought it was R900 a month. It was R2 300 with water.

No bank login needed.
